complexity.notes: The guard `s[i+length-1] in s[i:i+length]` is always true when length > 0 (a character is trivially inside the window that ends on it), so it only serves to skip the decrement at length 0; `length = max(0, length - 1)` says the same thing without the scan. Each membership test also materializes a fresh slice copy of the window, so the per-step cost is paid twice and worst-case auxiliary space is the window size rather than O(1). On inputs whose duplicate-free windows grow with n the repeated linear scans make this quadratic; an O(n) version exists using ||a map of each character's most recent index, moving a left pointer directly past the previous occurrence instead of rescanning the window||.
complexity.summary: Sliding window whose length carries over between starting positions: each iteration shrinks the window by one (when nonempty) and greedily re-extends it, testing each candidate character with a linear `in` scan over a slice of the current window. An early break stops once the remaining suffix is too short to beat the best length found.
